prerequisites: Knowledge of basic mathematics, technical mechanics, and electrical engineering (DC and AC technology)
Fundamentals of analog and digital electronics

learning_outcomes.text: Evaluate and apply the fundamentals of metrology (accuracy, resolution, repeatability, error).
Discuss and evaluate influences on measurement results such as EMC and cross-sensitivities.
Know the application of appropriate remedial measures.
Competently evaluate the suitability of various sensors for typical applications in industrial processes, e.g., for measuring temperature, pressure, force, displacement, angle, and acceleration.
Explain and evaluate interference influences on sensor output signals.
Explain and evaluate typical signal conditioning and signal transmission of analog and digital sensor signals (interfaces) for applications.
Derive and evaluate metrological aspects such as errors.
Perform basic calculations of permanent and electromagnetic circuits, including with the Finite Element Method.
Understand the principles of electromagnetic force generation and apply them to force calculation.
Be familiar with the designs, functionalities, and mathematical models of electromagnets and permanent-magnet excited DC motors, as well as series-wound and universal motors.

Understand the functional parameters of sensors, evaluate them metrologically considering essential influencing parameters, describe sensors system-theoretically to analyze sensor systems, and apply them in concepts with sensors and actuators.
Analyze electromagnetic circuits and develop new functional concepts by considering and applying the fundamental findings described above in the development of electric motors.

syllabus_topics: Accuracy, resolution, linearity, reproducibility, and error analysis
Interfering variables influencing sensor output signals (EMC)
Electronic signal conditioning (analog electronics) and forwarding
Presentation and comparison of different interfaces
Evaluation of measurement results in connection with analog circuit technology and LTSPICE simulation
Brushed and brushless permanent-magnet excited DC motors
Design and optimization of electromagnetic actuators with the Finite Element Method
assessment_rules: The module grade for MECB650 corresponds to the module examination grade, which consists of two equal parts from MECB651 and MECB653. MECB652 Sensorics Lab is evaluated as a course achievement based on reports to be prepared for the individual experiments without grading.
